# LoadMargin

> Load profitability checks and DOT compliance reviews for U.S. owner-operators and small fleets. One person does the work and everything is arranged by email. The calculators and guides on the site are free and need no account.

LoadMargin is run by Aleksandar Novaković from Smederevo, Serbia. Payment is by PayPal invoice. Calculators run in the browser and nothing a visitor enters is uploaded.

## Services

- [Services and prices](https://loadmargin.com/work.html): Quick Load Check $49 (one load checked against the carrier's own costs, one-page PDF, refund available), Full Cost & Lane Audit $249, Authority Checklist Review $99, New Authority Setup $349, Compliance Tune-up $199, Load Check Plan $99 a month, Ongoing Support $249 to $799 a month.
- [Sample Quick Load Check report](https://loadmargin.com/sample-load-check-report.pdf): what the one-page report looks like.
- [How it works](https://loadmargin.com/how-it-works.html): The exact formula behind every LoadMargin verdict and what each of the eight free console modules does.

## Free calculators

- [Load calculator](https://loadmargin.com/load-calculator.html): Free trucking load calculator: enter rate, loaded and deadhead miles, diesel, driver pay and fixed costs to see profit, margin and rate per mile. No sign-up.
- [DOT audit readiness check](https://loadmargin.com/audit-check.html): Free self-check for small US carriers: score your new-entrant or safety audit readiness across driver files, drug testing, HOS and records. Nothing uploaded.
- [Trucking cost per mile calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-cost-per-mile.html): Free trucking cost per mile calculator: fixed costs, fuel at today's diesel, driver pay and maintenance in one number, plus your break-even and target rate.
- [Deadhead and backhaul calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-deadhead.html): Free deadhead calculator for truckers: what empty miles cost, the real rate per total mile, and whether a cheap backhaul beats driving home empty.
- [Detention pay calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-detention.html): Free detention calculator: what an hour waiting at a dock really costs a truck, how much detention pay covers, and how to price slow facilities.
- [HOS and ETA calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-eta.html): Free hours-of-service calculator: arrival time, the 30-minute break, the 11-hour and 14-hour limits, and the farthest you can legally drive now.
- [Freight factoring fee calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-factoring.html): Free freight factoring calculator: monthly cost, effective rate and annual percentage rate of factoring fees, per-invoice charges and monthly minimums.
- [Truck fuel cost calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-fuel-cost.html): Free truck fuel cost calculator: gallons and diesel cost for a trip, including empty miles and idling, fuel cost per mile, and what $0.50 more diesel does.
- [Trucking fuel surcharge calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-fuel-surcharge.html): Free trucking fuel surcharge calculator: surcharge per mile from the DOE diesel price, base and peg MPG, and how much of your real fuel it covers.
- [IFTA calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-ifta.html): Free IFTA calculator: estimate your quarterly fuel tax by state from miles and gallons, with fleet MPG, taxable gallons and net tax due or credit.
- [Truck maintenance cost per mile calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-maintenance.html): Free truck maintenance cost per mile calculator: turn 12 months of repairs and tires into a per-mile reserve and a monthly amount to set aside.
- [Truck driver per diem calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-per-diem.html): Free truck driver per diem calculator: days away at the IRS $80 rate, the 80% deductible share, and roughly how much tax it saves an owner-operator.
- [Owner-operator take-home pay calculator](https://loadmargin.com/calc-take-home.html): Free owner-operator take-home pay calculator: yearly revenue minus fuel, maintenance, truck payments, insurance and tax, plus your break-even rate.
- [Trip safety check](https://loadmargin.com/calc-trip-safety.html): Free pre-trip safety check for truckers: hours of service, sleep, night driving, weather and route risks, with red and green flags before you take a load.
- [All calculators](https://loadmargin.com/calculators.html): Free trucking calculators for owner-operators: deadhead, fuel surcharge, detention, HOS, IFTA, factoring, maintenance and take-home pay. No sign-up.

## Guides

- [Form 2290, and the stamp you cannot register without](https://loadmargin.com/guide-2290-hvut.html): The federal road tax every 55,000-lb-plus truck pays: $550 a year at 80,000 lb, due 31 August, and the stamped Schedule 1 you cannot register a plate without.
- [Accessorials, the charges you keep forgetting to bill](https://loadmargin.com/guide-accessorials.html): Detention is only the start: layover, TONU, lumper, extra stops, driver assist, redelivery and more.
- [After a crash, the sequence that protects you](https://loadmargin.com/guide-accident-procedures.html): The minutes after a truck crash decide the claim: the safety-first sequence, the photos and notes that protect you, the required drug test and the reporting.
- [Trucking associations, and whether the dues pay](https://loadmargin.com/guide-associations.html): What OOIDA and state trucking associations offer an owner-operator: advocacy, education, benefits and discounts, and when a membership actually pays.
- [What authority really costs](https://loadmargin.com/guide-authority.html): The itemised cost of US operating authority, why insurance is 70-80% of the bill, three realistic first-year totals and the working capital nobody budgets.
- [Vetting brokers, and the fifteen minutes that pays for itself](https://loadmargin.com/guide-broker-fraud.html): Double brokering and identity theft cost carriers up to $1bn a year. A fifteen-minute broker vetting routine, reading SAFER, and what to do if it goes wrong.
- [Getting set up with brokers, the first time and fast](https://loadmargin.com/guide-broker-setup.html): What a freight broker needs before handing you a load: the carrier packet, authority and insurance filings, and the setup that makes you easy to book.
- [Banking and books, the habit that pays for itself](https://loadmargin.com/guide-business-banking.html): The separate account, clean books and receipt habits that keep your trucking LLC protection real, your taxes lower and your cost per mile honest.
- [Business credit, and why year two is cheaper than year one](https://loadmargin.com/guide-business-credit.html): Why a new carrier gets financed like a risk, how to build business credit of its own, and the small steps that mean better truck rates and lower deposits.
- [How to structure a carrier, without the myths](https://loadmargin.com/guide-business-structure.html): Why almost every carrier runs an LLC, what it does and does not protect, when the S-corp election saves self-employment tax, and the EIN and banking.
- [Buying a truck without buying a problem](https://loadmargin.com/guide-buying-a-truck.html): New vs used semi trucks, down payments and rates for a new authority, the pre-purchase inspection, and why the cheapest truck is often the costliest to own.
- [Cargo claims, and the two minutes at pickup](https://loadmargin.com/guide-cargo-claims.html): How cargo claims work: what the claimant must prove, the five carrier defences, the deadlines, released value, and how to document a pickup to stop a claim.
- [Cargo theft, the load that vanishes without a break-in](https://loadmargin.com/guide-cargo-theft.html): Strategic cargo theft and fictitious pickups: how loads get stolen without a break-in, which freight thieves target, and the habits that protect your authority.
- [Choosing an ELD you will not regret](https://loadmargin.com/guide-choosing-eld.html): How to choose an ELD: the FMCSA registration and delisting risk, contract traps, the data transfer methods inspectors ask for, and features worth paying for.
- [The Clearinghouse, and the query due every January](https://loadmargin.com/guide-clearinghouse.html): The FMCSA Drug & Alcohol Clearinghouse for owner-operators: the annual query due 5 January, Clearinghouse II CDL downgrades and the return-to-duty process.
- [The audits that come after the first one](https://loadmargin.com/guide-compliance-review.html): What triggers an FMCSA compliance review or focused investigation after your first 18 months, what a safety rating means, and how to stay audit-ready.
- [How to calculate your true cost per mile](https://loadmargin.com/guide-cost-per-mile.html): The step-by-step method for working out what a mile costs your truck, why most carriers are 15-25 cents wrong, and how to use the number on a real load.
- [CSA scores, and what they really cost](https://loadmargin.com/guide-csa.html): A CSA score is a percentile, not a grade. The seven BASICs, intervention thresholds, severity and time weighting, and what crossing one costs in insurance.
- [DataQs, and getting a wrong violation off your record](https://loadmargin.com/guide-dataqs.html): A wrong roadside violation stays on your CSA and your insurance for two years unless you challenge it.
- [The real cost of deadhead miles](https://loadmargin.com/guide-deadhead.html): Why deadhead miles are the most misread number in freight, what an empty mile really costs, and how to price a backhaul so a cheap return is judged right.
- [The emissions system, and the repair that ambushes owners](https://loadmargin.com/guide-def-dpf.html): How DPF, regen, DEF and SCR keep a modern diesel legal, how they fail, what repairs cost, and why a neglected emissions system is a five-figure surprise.
- [Depreciation, and the deduction that can backfire](https://loadmargin.com/guide-depreciation.html): How truck depreciation works for owner-operators: Section 179, bonus and regular depreciation, why the biggest deduction is not always best, and what to ask.
- [Detention, and the hour you cannot bill for](https://loadmargin.com/guide-detention.html): Detention pay covers about a quarter of what a detained hour costs. The full arithmetic, accessorials carriers leave unbilled, and how to price dwell risk.
- [A dispatcher, or do it yourself?](https://loadmargin.com/guide-dispatcher.html): What a truck dispatcher does, what the 5-10% fee costs per mile, the case for and against, and how to spot one who earns the cut versus one who books cheap.
- [The DOT physical, and the card you cannot drive without](https://loadmargin.com/guide-dot-physical.html): The DOT physical: what the exam checks, conditions that shorten or threaten your medical card, how it ties to your CDL, and the lapse that sidelines you.
- [Driver pay, and who carries the bad day](https://loadmargin.com/guide-driver-pay.html): Truck driver pay models compared: per mile, percentage, hourly and salary, what each does to cost per mile, and the employer burden that turns $0.62 into $0.85.
- [The drug and alcohol program, the part behind the database](https://loadmargin.com/guide-drug-alcohol-program.html): The DOT drug and alcohol program every carrier must run: the consortium, six test types, written policy, supervisor training and the records to keep.
- [ELD rules, and the exemptions people get wrong](https://loadmargin.com/guide-eld.html): Who must run an ELD and who is exempt: the 150 air-mile short-haul test, the non-CDL 100-mile rule, eight days in thirty, and the pre-2000 engine exemption.
- [Estimated taxes, the bill that comes four times a year](https://loadmargin.com/guide-estimated-taxes.html): Quarterly estimated taxes for owner-operators: the IRS due dates, how to estimate, the safe-harbor rule that avoids penalties, and a separate tax account.
- [Factoring, and the price of forty days](https://loadmargin.com/guide-factoring.html): What freight factoring really costs once annualised, why a 1.5% offer can cost more than 3%, what non-recourse covers, and the question that decides it.
- [Buying fuel, net of tax](https://loadmargin.com/guide-fuel-buying.html): How to buy diesel cheaper: compare fuel net of state tax under IFTA, retail-minus vs cost-plus fuel cards, the break-even detour formula and idling cost.
- [Fuel cards, and the discount that is not always a discount](https://loadmargin.com/guide-fuel-cards.html): What a trucking fuel card really saves: network discounts, the retail-minus vs cost-plus trap, fees that eat the discount, and how to compare cards fairly.
- [Fuel surcharges, and the number nobody negotiates](https://loadmargin.com/guide-fuel-surcharge.html): How a fuel surcharge is calculated, what the DOE weekly diesel index measures, how the peg mpg moves thousands of dollars, and why it never covers all fuel.
- [Getting your authority, step by step](https://loadmargin.com/guide-get-authority.html): USDOT and operating authority, BOC-3, insurance filings, UCR and 2290: the filings in order, plus the 2026 registration changes that are still settling.
- [Hazmat, the premium and what it asks in return](https://loadmargin.com/guide-hazmat.html): Is hauling hazmat worth it? The endorsement and TSA check, placards and shipping papers, the security plan, and the higher stakes behind the higher rate.
- [Health insurance, the benefit nobody hands you now](https://loadmargin.com/guide-health-insurance.html): Health insurance for owner-operators: why it belongs in your cost per mile, the routes to coverage when self-employed, and the deduction worth asking about.
- [The second truck is a different business](https://loadmargin.com/guide-hiring-first-driver.html): Hiring your first truck driver: the driver qualification file, payroll and pay model, insurance and CSA impact, and why truck two is a different business.
- [Hours of service, in plain English](https://loadmargin.com/guide-hos.html): The four HOS clocks explained: the 11-hour driving limit, 14-hour window, 30-minute break and 70-hour cycle, and why an illegal load is never a profitable one.
- [Hotshot trucking, and whether the math works](https://loadmargin.com/guide-hotshot.html): Hotshot trucking with a one-ton and a gooseneck: lower entry cost, lower rates, the payload ceiling, and whether it nets more than a used semi.
- [IFTA, without the folklore](https://loadmargin.com/guide-ifta.html): IFTA explained: the three-step calculation, a fully worked quarter, taxable versus total miles, the records an auditor asks for, and the cost of a bad audit.
- [Insurance, and the year before the quote](https://loadmargin.com/guide-insurance.html): Commercial truck insurance explained: each coverage, 2026 premium ranges, what moves a premium, why a lapse hurts more than a claim, and how to lower it.
- [IRP, the plate that bills you by where you drive](https://loadmargin.com/guide-irp-plates.html): IRP apportioned plates: how the registration fee is split across the states you run, estimated first-year vs actual renewal, and the mileage records you need.
- [Lease-purchase, and the nine clauses that decide it](https://loadmargin.com/guide-lease-purchase.html): A lease-purchase can be a real route to ownership or a treadmill, and the difference is about nine clauses.
- [Finding loads, without living on the board](https://loadmargin.com/guide-load-boards.html): How freight reaches an owner-operator: load boards, broker relationships and shipper-direct, what each costs, and why the cheapest-looking load rarely pays.
- [Load securement, where the rate premium is earned](https://loadmargin.com/guide-load-securement.html): Cargo securement rules: working load limit math for straps and chains, the aggregate rule, the required en-route checks, and why it is a life-safety issue.
- [Maintenance is a reserve, not an invoice](https://loadmargin.com/guide-maintenance.html): Truck maintenance cost per mile: a twelve-month rolling budget, what big repairs really cost, why a $2,400 breakdown costs $5,295, and how truck age moves it.
- [The MCS-150, the update that keeps you legal](https://loadmargin.com/guide-mcs150.html): The MCS-150 biennial update that keeps your USDOT number active: the schedule set by your DOT digits, deactivation and fines if missed, and your UCR bracket.
- [Negotiating with numbers](https://loadmargin.com/guide-negotiation.html): How to negotiate freight rates: your walk-away number, why target rate is a division, what to say and never say, and when a cheap load is the right call.
- [The new entrant audit, and the empty folder](https://loadmargin.com/guide-new-entrant-audit.html): How to pass the FMCSA new entrant safety audit: the sixteen automatic failures, the four files the auditor asks for, deadlines, and a ninety-day plan.
- [Four ways to run the same truck](https://loadmargin.com/guide-operating-models.html): Solo vs team, power-only, drop-and-hook, regional vs OTR vs local: four ways to run a truck and what each does to miles, home time and cost per mile.
- [Owner-operator or company driver, on the real numbers](https://loadmargin.com/guide-owner-vs-company.html): The decision that reshapes your income and your risk: higher gross against real costs and no benefits, freedom against responsibility.
- [Preventive maintenance on a schedule](https://loadmargin.com/guide-pm-schedule.html): A truck preventive maintenance schedule: daily, weekly and mileage-based checks, the annual DOT inspection, and why the pre-trip is the cheapest repair.
- [Quick pay vs factoring, getting paid before day 30](https://loadmargin.com/guide-quick-pay.html): Broker quick pay vs factoring: what each really costs, when each makes sense, and why the cheapest way to get paid faster depends on your cash flow.
- [The rate confirmation, line by line](https://loadmargin.com/guide-rate-confirmation.html): The rate confirmation is the contract for the load: what every line means, clauses that move risk onto you, and the check that prevents payment disputes.
- [Retirement, the plan nobody sets up for you now](https://loadmargin.com/guide-retirement.html): Retirement for owner-operators with no 401(k) match: SEP-IRA, Solo 401(k) and IRA options for self-employed drivers, and why the truck is not a plan.
- [The roadside inspection, and what it costs later](https://loadmargin.com/guide-roadside-inspection.html): CVSA roadside inspection levels, what an officer checks, the out-of-service items that strand you, and how inspections follow you into CSA and insurance.
- [The freight calendar, and planning around it](https://loadmargin.com/guide-seasonality.html): Why freight has a calendar: the slow first quarter, produce season and peak shipping, and how to plan cash, maintenance and time off around it.
- [Spot vs contract, the two markets you sell into](https://loadmargin.com/guide-spot-vs-contract.html): Spot vs contract freight: how the two markets' rates move against each other and how a small carrier balances spot freedom with contract stability.
- [Tax, and the money that was never yours](https://loadmargin.com/guide-taxes.html): Owner-operator taxes: 15.3% self-employment tax, quarterly estimates and safe harbor, the per diem drivers underclaim, deductions, and when an S-corp pays.
- [Tires, in cents per mile](https://loadmargin.com/guide-tires.html): Truck tire costs in cents per mile: why cheap tires are often expensive, the pressure and alignment habits that add miles, and when retreads make sense.
- [Dry van, reefer or flatbed: choosing on the real numbers](https://loadmargin.com/guide-trailer-types.html): Dry van vs reefer vs flatbed compared on what decides income: rate, cost, skill, claim risk and how easy the freight is to find.
- [Trip planning, where miles are won before you drive them](https://loadmargin.com/guide-trip-planning.html): Truck trip planning: fuel stops net of tax, parking before you run out of hours, appointment math on the 14-hour clock, and a trip that fits HOS rules.
- [UCR, the $46 filing that stops you at the scale](https://loadmargin.com/guide-ucr.html): The annual interstate fee almost nobody budgets: $46 for an owner-operator, due by 31 December, and a roadside violation if you skip it.
- [Weigh stations, and the bypass that saves you time](https://loadmargin.com/guide-weigh-stations.html): What happens at a weigh station, when you get pulled in for inspection, how bypass services work and whether they pay, and why a clean truck wants the scale.
- [Weight, axles and the ninety-second fix](https://loadmargin.com/guide-weight.html): Truck weight limits: the three federal limits, the bridge formula, how far to slide the tandems, fuel weight, and what an overweight ticket really costs.
- [Winter, and the trip that should not have been made](https://loadmargin.com/guide-winter-operations.html): Winter trucking: chain laws and when they apply, fuel gelling and winterised diesel, the cold-weather pre-trip, and when to stop instead of pushing on.
